label: input token t at one of the first three original positions
explanation: Fires only when the input token is the letter t at original positions 0, 1 or 2 (every activation has in_tok = t). It does not fire on t at position 3 or later (a handful of weak activations at t=3), on the delimiter, during the copy phase, or on any other token. Magnitude depends on position: t at position 0 gives about 0.9 (roughly 0.56 of max), and positions 1-2 give about 1.2-1.6. The largest activations (max 1.614) come from t at position 1 right after i. A repeated t gets slightly less (e.g. 0.8 of max for a second t at position 2). Lowest-quartile activations are faint traces at position 3, or at a copy step where t is output.

issues: I found no systematic counterexample. On the test split the predicate has 0 false positives: precision 1.0, recall 0.991, F1 0.995, mass recall 0.999.

The 464 missed test activations hold only 0.1% of the activation mass. Almost all are faint t inputs at position 3 (about 0.03-0.05 of max), plus a few traces at copy steps (dev split: 18 copy steps, all with t fed back as input, about 0.05-0.08 of max). This is what the explanation says, and these are too weak to be a gap worth fixing.

The magnitude claims hold up. Every top example is i at position 0 followed by t at position 1 (1.614 = 1.00 of max). t at position 0 gives exactly 0.898 (0.56 of max). From the mass shares, the average at position 1 is about 1.5 and at position 2 about 1.25. A repeated t ('i t t') gives 0.80 of max, confirming 'slightly less'.

Every activation has in_tok = t (lift 32.5x, all activation mass). The delimiter never fires (0 activations) and the copy phase is effectively silent, so the label does not overclaim compared with the predicate.
